title: Console (Beta) — Optimize Suggestions View UX Spec
author: Tessa Morgan
content:
## Overview
This document specifies the Redwood Console “Suggestions” view (beta) for Redwood Optimize. The view surfaces automated recommendations (initially batching + caching) with:
- Clear estimated savings (with basis and uncertainty).
- A risk level (Low/Medium/High) with concrete rationale.
- Filters and scoping by route/model/region.
- Read-only beta behavior (no one-click apply in phase 1), gated via feature flags and allowlisting.

This UX spec is intended to be implementable by Console engineering and consistent with the risk taxonomy (ADR-0274) and savings contract (ADR-0275).

## Goals
1) Make recommendations actionable: users can understand what to change, where it applies, and why it helps.
2) Make estimates trustworthy: present “estimated” savings with a visible basis, data recency, and uncertainty.
3) Support safe adoption: risk is explicit, explained, and tied to reversibility/guardrails.
4) Scale to large tenants: pagination, filtering, and stable list performance.

## Non-goals (Beta phase 1)
- No “Apply” action or configuration write-backs.
- No in-console experimentation setup (A/B, canary) beyond linking to existing Rollouts tooling.
- No manual what-if simulator.

## Primary personas and use cases
### Persona A: Platform/ML engineer
- Wants to reduce unit cost ($/1M tokens) without breaking latency SLOs.
- Needs to know what telemetry/assumptions drive savings.

### Persona B: CS/SE / TAM
- Uses Suggestions during onboarding and QBRs.
- Needs defensible language: “estimated”, not “guaranteed”, plus easy-to-explain rationale.

## Information architecture (IA)
### Navigation placement
- Console left nav: **Optimize** (top-level)
  - **Suggestions (Beta)** (new sub-item)

Rationale: Suggestions is an Optimize surface, but must remain discoverable without implying automatic application.

### Page-level structure
**Suggestions (Beta)** page (full page):
1) Page header
2) Filters bar
3) Suggestions table (list)
4) Footer with pagination

### Deep link structure
- /optimize/suggestions
- /optimize/suggestions?suggestionId=<id> (opens detail drawer)

This supports sharing a specific suggestion with CS/SE and internal debugging.

## Feature gating and access
### Feature flags
- suggestions_beta (server + client)
- allowlist by tenant/workspace

### RBAC
- View access requires existing Optimize/Cost visibility permissions.
- If user lacks permission: show access denied state (see Empty/Error states).

### Audit logging (view-only)
- Log events when a suggestion detail is opened (not on list render) to reduce noise.

## Suggestions list: table spec
### Default sort
- Sort by **Estimated monthly savings (median)** descending.
- Tie-breaker: risk level ascending (Low before Medium before High).

### Table columns
1) **Suggestion**
   - Title (short imperative): e.g., “Increase max continuous batch size” / “Enable prefix caching on route”
   - Subtitle: scope summary (Route • Model • Region)
2) **Type**
   - Chip: Batching | Caching (future: Quantization, Routing)
3) **Scope**
   - Compact scope string; hover/tooltip shows full scope details:
     - Route: <route_name>
     - Model: <model_id or alias>
     - Region: <region>
4) **Estimated savings**
   - Primary: “$X / 1M tokens” (median)
   - Secondary: “~$Y / month” (median) based on recent volume
   - Tertiary (small): “Range: $A–$B / month” or “90% range: …” (see Savings disclosure)
5) **Risk**
   - Risk chip: Low / Medium / High
   - Hover reveals 1–2 top rationale bullets (first two in rationale list)
6) **Last updated**
   - Relative time (e.g., “6h ago”), tooltip shows absolute timestamp and data window

### Row interaction
- Clicking a row opens the detail drawer.
- Cmd/Ctrl-click opens the deep link with drawer pre-opened.

### Filters bar
Filters are additive (AND). All filters are optional.

1) Search
- Placeholder: “Search suggestions, routes, models”
- Matches: suggestion title, route name, model alias/id

2) Type
- Multi-select: Batching, Caching

3) Risk
- Multi-select: Low, Medium, High

4) Route
- Single-select dropdown (typeahead). Displays route label and internal route id.

5) Model
- Single-select dropdown (typeahead). Displays model alias + version when available.

6) Region
- Single-select dropdown. Includes “All regions” option.

7) Data readiness (beta)
- Toggle: “Show only suggestions with sufficient telemetry”
- Default: ON
- If OFF, include suggestions that exist but are flagged as “insufficient telemetry” (still read-only), primarily for internal/support debugging.

### Pagination
- Cursor-based pagination.
- Page size: 25 rows.
- Controls: Prev / Next with “Showing 1–25 of many” when total is unknown.

### Loading and refresh
- Initial load: skeleton rows (10) + disabled filters.
- Filter change: keep table chrome; show inline spinner in table header, maintain previous data until new results arrive (avoid empty flash).
- Background refresh: if data changes while user is on page, show non-blocking banner: “Suggestions updated. Refresh” (manual refresh).

## Suggestion detail drawer: content and hierarchy
### Drawer behavior
- Right-side drawer, 560–640px width.
- Supports scrolling inside drawer; page behind remains static.
- Close actions: X, Esc, clicking outside.

### Drawer header
- Title (same as row title)
- Type chip (Batching/Caching)
- Risk chip (Low/Medium/High)
- Status note (beta): “Read-only in beta”

### Section 1: What to change (action summary)
Purpose: Provide an implementable next step without “Apply”.

Contents:
- “Recommended change” (1–2 sentences)
- “Where this applies” bullets:
  - Route
  - Model
  - Region
  - Environment (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) if relevant
- “Expected impact” bullets (short): cost, latency, reliability

### Section 2: Estimated savings (primary disclosure)
Purpose: Make savings visible but clearly estimated.

Display pattern:
- Primary metric (large): “Estimated savings: $X / 1M tokens”
- Secondary: “Estimated monthly impact: ~$Y / month”
- Range: “Likely range: $A–$B / month”
- Data window + recency line: “Based on last 7 days of traffic. Updated 6h ago.”

Optional breakdown (collapsed by default):
- “How we computed this” (accordion)
  - Baseline cost: $/1M tokens
  - Projected cost after change: $/1M tokens
  - Assumed traffic volume: tokens/month
  - Notes on double-counting prevention (batching vs caching) when relevant

### Section 3: Risk and rationale (required)
Purpose: Provide concrete reasons for the risk label without overpromising.

Display pattern:
- Risk chip + one-line definition
- “Why this is <Low/Medium/High> risk” bullets (3–6 bullets)
  - Examples (copy-level, not implementation-level):
    - “Traffic has high variance in request size; batching improvements may be less stable.”
    - “Latency headroom is limited on this route; batching changes could increase p95.”
    - “Cache hit-rate estimate has low confidence due to limited repeated prefixes.”
- “How to validate safely” (short guidance)
  - Link: “Open Rollouts” (existing workflow)
  - Suggested measurement window (e.g., 2–24h depending on risk)

### Section 4: Basis of estimate (telemetry + assumptions)
Purpose: “Trust but verify.” This section is the user-visible answer to “what data did you use?”.

Required fields to render (as human text):
- Traffic window: “last N days”
- Sample size: “N requests / N tokens” (rounded)
- Token distribution summary: “p50/p95 input tokens, p50/p95 output tokens” (if available)
- Current settings detected: e.g., batching enabled/disabled, cache enabled/disabled, relevant knobs as read-only
- Exclusions/guardrails applied: e.g., “Suppressed for long-context > 16k” (if applicable)

Presentation:
- Use a compact two-column list (Label | Value).
- For advanced metrics, keep behind “Show details”.

### Section 5: Notes and limitations (beta)
- “This is an estimate; realized savings depend on workload and traffic mix.”
- “No configuration changes are made automatically in beta.”
- “If your traffic changes, savings may change week-to-week.”

### Footer actions
Phase 1 (beta read-only):
- Primary button: “Copy link”
- Secondary: “Export details” (optional; default OFF for beta; see Security)
- Tertiary link: “Give feedback” (opens feedback modal with suggestionId)

Phase 2 (future, not implemented):
- “Apply change” (with guardrails, rollback, and permissions)

## Risk chip: visual language and copy
### Visual spec
- Low: neutral/positive styling (green or success)
- Medium: warning styling (amber)
- High: critical styling (red)

Accessibility:
- Do not rely on color alone; include label text.
- Provide aria-label: “Risk level: High. May impact latency or quality.”

### Copy definitions (tooltip)
- Low: “Unlikely to impact latency/quality. Easy to revert.”
- Medium: “May impact latency or quality in some workloads. Validate with a rollout.”
- High: “More likely to impact SLOs or quality, or the estimate is less stable. Validate carefully before adopting.”

## Savings disclosure: “estimated” vs “guaranteed”
### Required language
- Always use **Estimated** (never “Guaranteed”, “Will save”, “You will reduce cost by”).
- Use probabilistic framing for ranges: “Likely range”, “Expected range”, “90% range” (depending on contract).

### Prohibited language
- “Guaranteed savings”
- “Zero risk”
- “No impact on latency/quality” (unless specifically validated and approved wording exists; beta does not include such claims)

### Recommended phrases
- “Estimated savings”
- “Based on recent traffic”
- “Results may vary by workload”
- “Validate with a canary rollout”

### Example copy blocks
1) List column (compact):
- “$18 / 1M tokens”
- “~$2,100 / month”
- Tooltip: “Estimated. Based on last 7 days. Likely range: $1,500–$2,800 / month.”

2) Drawer primary line:
- “Estimated monthly impact: ~$2,100 / month (likely range $1,500–$2,800)”

## Empty, error, and edge states
### 1) No suggestions (true empty)
Condition: API returns zero suggestions with sufficient telemetry.

UI:
- Title: “No suggestions yet”
- Body:
  - “We’ll show recommendations once we have enough recent traffic for this workspace.”
- Guidance bullets:
  - “Check that traffic is flowing through a route with logging enabled.”
  - “Try widening your date window (if available) or return later.”
- Link: “Learn what telemetry is required” (docs)

### 2) Feature not enabled (allowlist / flag)
Condition: suggestions_beta false.

UI:
- Title: “Suggestions (Beta) isn’t enabled for this workspace”
- Body:
  - “Contact your Redwood team to request access.”
- Button: “Request enablement” (opens support form / mailto with workspace id)

### 3) Access denied (RBAC)
Condition: user lacks permission.

UI:
- Title: “You don’t have access to Suggestions”
- Body:
  - “Ask a workspace admin to grant Optimize visibility permissions.”

### 4) Insufficient telemetry (partial data)
Condition: suggestion exists but missing required baselines.

List behavior:
- Default: hide these suggestions (Data readiness toggle ON).
- If shown: render savings as “—” and include badge “Insufficient telemetry”.

Drawer behavior:
- Savings section shows:
  - “Estimated savings unavailable”
  - “Reason: Missing recent baseline cost metrics for this route/model.”
  - “What to do: Ensure token metering is enabled and traffic is present.”

### 5) Stale data
Condition: baselines older than freshness threshold.

UI:
- Banner in drawer: “Data may be stale (last updated 3d ago). Savings may be inaccurate.”
- Still show risk + rationale; show savings but de-emphasize (smaller, muted) and keep “stale” warning visible.

### 6) API error
- Page-level error state with retry.
- Provide support/debug info (copy button): requestId, workspaceId, timestamp.

## Copy and terminology guidelines
### Terminology
- Use “route” consistently (not “endpoint”) in the Suggestions UI.
- Use “model” and include version/alias where available.
- Use “region” aligned with Console region naming.

### Batching terminology
- Preferred: “continuous batching” where it’s the mechanism.
- In user-facing copy, say “batching” with an info tooltip: “Batching groups compatible requests to reduce GPU overhead.”

### Caching terminology
- Preferred: “prefix caching” (if the recommendation is prefix/KV cache reuse).
- Do not imply content caching of outputs unless that is explicitly what the system does.

### Tone
- Precise and cautious: avoid absolutes.
- Provide next-step guidance without prescribing unsafe actions.

## Accessibility and responsive behavior
- Table supports keyboard navigation; row focus state visible.
- Risk chips and savings tooltips must be accessible via keyboard.
- Drawer focus trap; Esc closes; close button has label.
- On narrow screens: table becomes stacked cards; drawer becomes full-screen modal.

## Analytics (UX instrumentation)
Tracked events must be privacy-safe and tenant-scoped. Do not include raw prompts or user content.

Required events:
- suggestions_list_viewed (workspaceId, filters summary, result_count)
- suggestion_opened (suggestionId, type, risk_level)
- filter_applied (filter keys only, no raw search text unless hashed)
- copy_link_clicked (suggestionId)
- feedback_submitted (suggestionId, rating, tags)

## Open questions / follow-ups
1) Whether to expose “confidence” as a separate label vs fold into Basis of estimate (current spec: fold into Basis).
2) Export details button: default OFF for beta pending security review of cost/usage exposure.
3) Date window selector (7d vs 30d): not in beta scope; revisit after telemetry freshness issues are resolved.

## Implementation notes (handoff)
- The list must render without total count (cursor pagination).
- The drawer must tolerate forward-compatible fields (schema versioning).
- Savings and risk sections must render independently; do not block risk display when savings is unavailable.

## Appendix: UI content checklist (Definition of Done)
- [ ] Suggestions appears in Optimize nav behind feature flag.
- [ ] List supports filters (type, risk, route, model, region) + search.
- [ ] Savings always labeled “Estimated” and includes range + data window in drawer.
- [ ] Risk chip always shown with rationale bullets.
- [ ] Empty states implemented (not enabled / no access / no suggestions / insufficient telemetry / stale / API error).
- [ ] Accessibility: keyboard nav, focus trap, aria labels.
- [ ] Analytics events implemented per above.
